headline: Chips Surge, Software and Housing Slide as Traders Eye a Busy Week
body_html:
Friday, November 6, ended with a lopsided market. Semiconductors jumped 5.23% as a group, while software lost 1.54%, consumer shares fell 1.63% and homebuilders dropped 2.10%. Of the 525 stocks we track, 236 rose and 287 fell, so decliners outnumbered gainers despite the strong chip session.

The semiconductor rally reached well beyond the usual leaders. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor climbed 27.76% and Diodes rose 13.17%. Networking and optical names joined in: Ubiquiti gained 15.29%, Extreme Networks 14.16% and Coherent 13.58%. TransMedics topped the board at 27.92%. Energy added 0.99%, materials 0.31% and industrials 0.09%. On the downside, BlackLine tumbled 23.11%, eXp World Holdings lost 20.72% and Artivion slid 20.21%.

Looking to the week ahead, Monday, November 9, is the first chance to see whether the chip leadership holds or fades. Investors will also follow the political aftermath of the midterm elections and a busy run of Middle East news. Reports of intercepted missiles near Riyadh, explosions in southern Iran and a disabled cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman sit behind energy's modest gain.

briefs.headline: Chip rally reaches the small-cap corners
briefs.body: Power and discrete semiconductor makers joined Friday's surge. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor rose 27.76% and Diodes gained 13.17%. The sector as a whole advanced 5.23%, the best showing of any group we track. Monday will test whether buyers stay engaged.

briefs.headline: Software takes a beating, led by BlackLine
briefs.body: BlackLine fell 23.11%, the steepest drop in our universe, and software as a group lost 1.54%. The slide ran against the chip rally and left the sector among the session's weakest. Traders will look for any sign of stabilization at the start of the week.

briefs.headline: Medical-device names split sharply
briefs.body: TransMedics soared 27.92%, the day's biggest gain, while Artivion dropped 20.21% and diagnostics firm Natera fell 14.59%. Healthcare overall slipped 0.15%, so sharp single-stock moves mostly offset each other beneath a quiet sector average.

briefs.headline: Gulf security headlines stay in focus
briefs.body: A Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh. Separately, Iranian media reported explosions in southern Iran, and the US military said it disabled a cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman. Energy shares rose a modest 0.99% on Friday.

briefs.headline: Israel's president turns to Netanyahu rival
briefs.body: Israel's president has asked Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of Prime Minister Netanyahu, to try to assemble a governing coalition. The outcome of that effort will be a political storyline to follow in the days ahead.

briefs.headline: Meta strategy chief departs for AI startup
briefs.body: Meta's chief strategy officer, Dave Wehner, is leaving to become chief financial officer at AI infrastructure startup Fireworks. The move is another sign of senior finance and strategy talent shifting toward fast-growing artificial-intelligence infrastructure companies.
